notice: SYNTHETIC EVALUATION DATA for comparing embedding providers. Written for RESQIVO; not official guidance from NDMA, WHO, UNDRR or any other organisation. Each query has exactly one relevant passage.

passages.text: Shelter teams keep drinking water in clean covered containers and log the litres handed out each day.
Coordinators compare occupancy with capacity twice daily and send arriving families to shelters with free space.
When a flooded road closes, the planning desk marks the route blocked and reassigns vehicles to another road.
Logistics, shelter and medical leads meet every six hours to report shortages and agree priorities.
First-aid kits are distributed to shelters in proportion to the number of people staying there.
Each camp needs enough latrines, kept clean and placed away from water points, to prevent disease.
Cooked meals and dry rations are distributed once a day, with extra portions for children and pregnant women.
Elderly residents and people with disabilities are registered first and given ground-floor sleeping areas.
Sirens and text messages alert villages when the river gauge passes the danger mark.
Diesel generators supply electricity for lighting and charging phones when the grid fails.
Volunteers sign in at the registration desk, receive an identity badge and are assigned a team.
Rescue boats and trained swimmers search submerged neighbourhoods for stranded residents.
Health workers record cases of fever and diarrhoea each day to spot outbreaks early.
During extreme heat, cooling centres open in schools and staff watch for signs of heat stroke.
Daily announcements in local languages tell families where to collect supplies.
A reunification desk records missing relatives and matches separated children with their parents.
